title: Platform Publication
description:
The status of one release on one platform. Publication is not atomic — Yandex can reject what CrazyGames approved — so each (release × platform) pair carries its own state, and the release computes its quorum from these.

The rejection path is the important one. A rejection MUST emit a compliance finding that versions the platform profile, either as a new assertion or an entry in review.common_rejections. A rejection that only sets a status field teaches the factory nothing, and the next title hits the same wall. This is the highest-return feedback loop in the system.

Since 1.1.0 the record also carries what the Factory's own publication steps established: a `readiness` (READY, BLOCKED, HUMAN_REQUIRED, UNKNOWN) computed at release:validating from the publication guards, an `outcome` of the last publication attempt at release:submitting, the `submission` method and its idempotency key and portal draft id, every piece of evidence (hashed, redacted), and a `measurement_class` saying who observed the portal state. `state` is set only from an observed portal state, never from the success of a click; a state the step could not observe stays where it was and the outcome says `UNKNOWN`. Every 1.1.0 field is optional, so a 1.0.0 record written by hand still validates.

state.description: The platform-publication machine's state. Advanced by an observed portal state or a person's record; never by a click that returned.

readiness.description: Since 1.1.0. What release:validating established about publishing this release here: READY (every publication guard GREEN and the package validated), BLOCKED (a guard RED, an assertion breached, a package missing), HUMAN_REQUIRED (publishable only by a person: no automated submission method, terms of automated console use unconfirmed, a credential nobody captured), UNKNOWN (a guard could not be evaluated). A publication step never proceeds on BLOCKED, HUMAN_REQUIRED or UNKNOWN; UNKNOWN is never read as READY.

guards.description: Since 1.1.0. The lifecycle guards release:validating evaluated for this platform (release.machine.yaml, platform-publication.machine.yaml), with their verdicts.

assertion_results.description: Results of running this platform profile's assertions against the built package. Every failure here names a rule, so remediation targets a known thing rather than 'platform validation failed'.

package.description: Since 1.1.0. The package this record is about, as the release manifest lists it and as validating found it on disk.

verified_on_disk.description: The file exists in the checkout and its sha256 equals `checksum`.

submission.description: How this release reaches the portal. Before 1.1.0: a human checklist plus this record. Since 1.1.0 the Factory's publish step may carry it out through a platform adapter - an API where the portal publishes one, a deterministic browser run of the portal's console where it does not - and records here what it did, keyed so that a second attempt finds the first.

method.description: Since 1.1.0. How the submission is made: api/cli through the portal's own tooling, console through a deterministic browser run of its developer console, email or manual by a person.

publication_profile_version.description: Since 1.1.0. The core/reference/publication/<platform-id>.yaml version the adapter followed.

idempotency_key.description: Since 1.1.0. Deterministic for (run, release manifest hash, platform). Written into the portal draft's name or note, and looked up before any upload, so a crash or retry finds the draft it already made.

portal_draft_id.description: Since 1.1.0. The draft, build or game id the portal assigned, read from the console or API after the upload; recorded before any submit.

dry_run.description: Since 1.1.0. True when the publish step stopped before the irreversible submit by policy (factory.publish.mode).

attempts.description: Since 1.1.0. Publication attempts made in this run for this platform.

authorized_by.description: Since 1.1.0. The G6 decision the submit was checked against: its artifact id and the release-manifest hash it pinned.

outcome.description: Since 1.1.0. The last publication attempt's result in the one vocabulary every adapter maps its platform's failures into. SUBMITTED means the portal was observed holding the submission; VERIFIED that its state was read back after; UNKNOWN that the portal state could not be observed - never a success.

human_required.description: Since 1.1.0. Present when a person must act before publication continues, and why. The step stopped here; it never worked around it.

resume_with.description: What a person does next, e.g. `wgf decide <run> done` after submitting by hand.

verified_state.description: Since 1.1.0. The portal's own state as the adapter read it back after acting - the only thing `state` is ever advanced from.

source.description: Where it was read: a console page's status text, an API response field.

evidence.description: Since 1.1.0. What was observed, hashed and redacted. A screenshot is cited by run-relative path and sha256; text read from the console is kept after redaction; nothing here ever carries a credential.

measurement_class.description: Since 1.1.0. Who observed what this record says: the validating step's deterministic checks, a browser run of the console, an API, or a person. A portal's moderation verdict is never an automation observation.

assertion_ids.description: Assertions that should have caught this. Empty means the profile had no rule for it — which is exactly the case that must produce a new one.

compliance_finding.description: How the platform profile changes so this cannot recur. Mandatory: this is what turns a rejection into institutional memory.
